Emergency Response Plan  

Amogy is committed to employee, public, and environmental safety.  This commitment is demonstrated by our comprehensive accidental release prevention program that covers areas such as design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training associated with the processes at our facility.  It is our policy to implement appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of regulated substances.  Under no circumstances will our personnel remain in a hazardous atmosphere beyond the acceptable limits of their safety equipment.  For emergency situations, Amogy will coordinate with local response organizations which provides emergency response expertise. 

  

Amogy has specific programs and practices in place for controlling this process to help ensure that a harmful release does not occur.  These programs and practices include: 

  

Use of and generally accepted recognized good engineering practices in the design, installation and operation of our equipment and ensuring this equipment meets applicable codes and standards. 

Continual assessment of hazards and safeguards in our process to reduce risks. 

Maintaining preparedness and contingency plans for responding to any emergency that may occur and coordinating these plans with local response agencies. 

Using EPA-approved methods and technology to analyze worst-case and alternative scenarios for the unlikely release of ammonia from the process. 

 

Amogy is continually seeking ways to improve the safety of our operations.  Consistent with that policy, our facility has been designed to include best practices in safety and environmental protection advancements.  Our Process Safety and Risk Management Procedures and Emergency Response Plan are in place and being used to manage hazards and control risks associated with hazardous materials at the facility. There will be annual reviews of the processes such as process hazard analysis, operating procedures, mechanical integrity

program, training, management of change, incident investigation. 

The Stationary Source and the Regulated Substances Handled 
Anhydrous ammonia is a toxic chemical to be stored at the Amogy site in two horizontal pressurized tanks.  The maximum quantity of ammonia to be stored on site is approximately 61,300 lbs.  

Hydrogen is a category 1 flammable gas stored at the Amogy site.  The total amount of hydrogen stored is below 10,000 pounds (approximately 7,500 lbs), however it is interconnected with the ammonia process and therefore subject to regulation under PSM and is included in the offsite consequence analysis under the Clean Air Act General Duty Clause. 

The Worst-Case Release Scenario(s) and the Alternative Release 
Worst case and alternate release scenarios were developed using the methodology given in the EPAs RMP*Comp program as well as the EPA Risk Management Program Guidance.  The details of the chosen scenarios will be included in the Risk Management Plan that will be available on site. 

Prevention & Emergency Response Policy 
Amogy is committed to employee, public, and environmental safety.  It is our policy to implement appropriate controls to prevent possible releases of regulated substances.  This commitment is demonstrated by our comprehensive accidental release prevention program that covers areas such as design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training associated with the processes at our facility.  It is Amogy policy to have a proactive approach to employee health and safety. To implement this, Amogy has instituted a comprehensive emergency response program that is coordinated with local response organizations.
